title: Caccetta-Häggkvist Conjecture (Conjecture 1)
statement_text: For all positive integers $n$, $r$, every simple $n$-vertex digraph with minimum outdegree at least $r$ contains a directed cycle of length at most $\lceil n/r \rceil$.
context_text: Proposed in 1978, this is a notoriously difficult open problem in directed graph theory. The case $r = n/3$ remains open despite considerable attention. Aharoni's Conjecture 3 is a graph-theoretic strengthening replacing directed cycles with rainbow cycles in an undirected setting.
paper_contribution: Proves the $r=2$ case of Aharoni's rainbow strengthening of this conjecture (Theorem 5), which implies the $r=2$ case of Caccetta-Häggkvist. Also introduces Conjecture 4, a weaker rainbow properly-coloured-cycle condition shown to imply the full Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture.

title: Aharoni's Conjecture (Conjecture 3)
statement_text: Let $G$ be a simple $n$-vertex graph and $c$ be a colouring of $E(G)$ with $n$ colours, where each colour class has size at least $r$. Then $(G, c)$ contains a rainbow cycle of length at most $\lceil n/r \rceil$.
context_text: Aharoni proposed this as a strengthening of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture, replacing directed cycles with rainbow cycles in an undirected graph. The paper's main result (Theorem 5) settles the $r=2$ case, which is described in the abstract as best possible.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for $r=2$ (Theorem 5): every simple $n$-vertex graph with a colouring of its edges by $n$ colours, each colour class of size at least 2, contains a rainbow cycle of length at most $\lceil n/2 \rceil$.

title: Conjecture 4
statement_text: Let $G$ be a simple $n$-vertex graph and $c$ be a colouring of $E(G)$ with $n$ colours, where each colour class has size at least $r$. Then $(G, c)$ contains a cycle $C$ of length at most $\lceil n/r \rceil$ such that no two incident edges of $C$ are the same colour.
context_text: A colouring $c$ of $E(G)$ is an arbitrary (not necessarily proper) assignment of colours to edges; a subgraph is rainbow if no two of its edges have the same colour. The Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture states that every simple $n$-vertex digraph (at most one arc from $u$ to $v$ for all $u,v$) with minimum outdegree at least $r$ has a directed cycle of length at most $\lceil n/r\rceil$; it is known for $r\le5$ but open in general, e.g. for $r=n/3$. Aharoni proposed the strengthening: if $G$ is a simple $n$-vertex graph and $c$ colours $E(G)$ with $n$ colours, each colour class of size at least $r$, then $(G,c)$ contains a rainbow cycle of length at most $\lceil n/r\rceil$. The present conjecture weakens rainbow to the condition that consecutive (incident) edges of the cycle have distinct colours. The authors show it still implies the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture: forget the orientations of a digraph on $[n]$ and colour the edge $ij$ with colour $i$ when $(i,j)$ is an arc; a cycle with no two incident edges of the same colour is then a directed cycle. The paper proves Aharoni's conjecture (hence this one) for $r=2$, which is best possible, and asks to prove either conjecture for $r\in\{3,4,5\}$.

title: Conjecture 12
statement_text: Let $M$ be a simple rank-$(n-1)$ matroid and $c$ be a colouring of $E(M)$ with $n$ colours, where each colour class has size at least $2$. Then $M$ contains a rainbow circuit of size at most $\lceil n/2 \rceil$.
context_text: A matroid $M$ on a finite ground set $E(M)$ is given by its circuits (nonempty, pairwise incomparable sets satisfying circuit elimination); a set is independent if it contains no circuit, the rank of $M$ is the size of a largest independent set, and $M$ is simple if it has no circuits of size 1 or 2. A colouring of $E(M)$ is arbitrary, and a circuit is rainbow if its elements have distinct colours. The graphic matroid $M(G)$ has the cycles of $G$ as circuits (rank $n-1$ for connected $n$-vertex $G$), and the cographic matroid has the minimal edge-cuts as circuits; a matroid is binary if representable over $GF(2)$ and regular if representable over every field. The conjecture is the matroid analogue of the authors' main theorem: if $G$ is a simple $n$-vertex graph and $E(G)$ is coloured with $n$ colours, each class of size at least $2$, then there is a rainbow cycle of length at most $\lceil n/2\rceil$. Thus it holds for graphic matroids, and the authors prove it for cographic matroids. However, the paper itself notes that the conjecture is false in general: the uniform matroid $U_{n-1,m}$ (rank $n-1$, every $n$-subset a circuit) has no circuit of size less than $n$; and it fails even for binary matroids: for each even $n\ge6$ there is a simple rank-$(n-1)$ binary matroid on $2n$ elements, coloured with classes of size 2, whose rainbow circuits all have size greater than $n/2$ (a forthcoming paper of Bai, Bowler and Huynh gives rank-$6n$ examples where the shortest rainbow circuit has size $4n$). The authors instead conjecture that it holds for regular matroids, via Seymour's decomposition theorem.
